title: The Structural Number of Parties: An Electoral-Outcome-Independent Baseline for Comparing Party-System Scale
abstract: arXiv:2611.24714v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: How many parties can a country structurally sustain? Standard measures such as the effective number of parties (ENP) cannot answer this question. They are descriptive and post hoc: they summarize competition only after an election, and they depend on electoral returns that are often missing, interrupted, or unreliable in many developing democracies, particularly in Africa. They also offer no common scale for comparing the size of party registers with realized electoral fragmentation. We introduce the Structural Number of Parties (SNP), an outcome-independent baseline derived from two universally available quantities: population size and territorial area. Building on the logic of the seat product model and the cube-root law of assembly size, the SNP gives an ex ante benchmark that can be computed for any country and year, including where electoral data are absent. translated_title: 政党结构数：一种独立于选举结果的政党体系规模比较基准
translated_abstract: 一个国家在结构上究竟能够容纳多少个政党？诸如有效政党数（ENP）等标准测量方法无法回答这个问题。它们是描述性的、事后性的：它们只能在选举之后概括竞争状况，并且依赖于选举得票数据，而在许多发展中民主国家（尤其是非洲国家），这类数据往往缺失、中断或不可靠。此外，这些方法也无法为比较政党登记规模与实际选举碎片化程度提供共同的尺度。我们提出了政党结构数，这是一个独立于选举结果的基准，仅由两个普遍可得的数据推导而来：人口规模和领土面积。基于席位乘积模型的逻辑和议会规模的立方根定律，SNP提供了一个可对任何国家和任何年份进行计算的事前基准，即使在没有选举数据的情况下也适用。将该指标应用于非洲国家，SNP能够进行结构性差距诊断……
tldr: 该论文提出了政党结构数（SNP），一种仅凭人口规模和领土面积即可计算、不依赖任何选举结果的事前基准，从而能够在缺乏选举数据的国家（尤其是非洲国家）衡量并比较政党体系的结构性规模。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Structural Number of Parties (SNP), an outcome-independent ex ante baseline derived solely from population size and territorial area, enabling structural diagnosis and comparison of party-system scale even in countries lacking reliable electoral data.
